# Bit-width study (supplementary, post-test; generated by scripts/analyze_quant_study.py)

How many bits does the decoder need, whatever chip runs it? Every archived final model (459: 17 conditions x 9 participants x 3 seeds) was rounded to a grid of weight and activation bit widths without retraining (post-training quantization, PTQ). Quantization-aware training (QAT) fine-tuned 4 architectures (full-22, relevance-16, relevance-16-prune50, relevance-8) for 100 more epochs with the rounding in the loop, next to a matched control fine-tuned for the same epochs without rounding (756 runs).

## How to read the numbers

- W/A means weight bits / activation bits, and float is 32-bit floating point: 4/8 is 4-bit weights with 8-bit activations. Weights are rounded per output channel; activations per tensor, over the range seen on the model's own session-1 training trials.
- Layers in order: input EEG, conv_t (temporal convolution), conv_s (spatial convolution), ELU, pooling, conv_d (depthwise convolution), conv_p (pointwise convolution), ELU, pooling, fc (classifier), logits. BatchNorm is folded into the convolutions, as in the exported graphs.
- Accuracy is on the artifact-free trials of session 2, the held-out day. Seeds are averaged within each participant (in pooled rows, the conditions too); then the nine participants are averaged.
- Differences are in percentage points (pp). Brackets hold the 95% participant bootstrap interval of the frozen plan (10,000 resamples, seed 690). 'Worst' is the participant who loses most; 'n > 2' counts the participants who lose more than 2 points.

## Boundaries

- Bit widths below 8 are simulated: weights and activations are rounded to integer grids and the network is evaluated in floating point (mibci.fakequant). No low-bit kernel was run or timed, so nothing here is about speed.
- All session-2 numbers are exploratory: the study was planned after the main study's test results were known.
- The precision rule (which tensors keep more bits) is read from session-1 sensitivity only. Session 2 only shows whether it carries over to the held-out day.
- Costs are counted from the network's shape, not measured. The energy figure counts arithmetic only, not memory traffic, and is an order-of-magnitude estimate.

## Key numbers

- The simulated 8/8 network agrees with the archived ONNX Runtime INT8 predictions on 99.29% of session-2 trials on average (lowest model 97.22%).
- Pooled over all conditions, against float/float: 8/8 -0.10 [-0.17, -0.03] pp, 4/8 -5.39 [-7.70, -3.43] pp, 4/4 -36.44 [-47.19, -25.74] pp; at 4/4, 9 of 9 participants lose more than 2 points.
- Narrowest setting at which no participant loses more than 2 points, pooled: 8/8 with equal widths, 6/8 with 8-bit activations.
- Session-1 rule: activations kept at 8 bits: input EEG, temporal convolution output, logits; weights kept above 2 bits: temporal convolution, spatial convolution, pointwise convolution, classifier. Rank correlation of the session-1 and session-2 sensitivities: +0.89.
- QAT, pooled over the QAT conditions, after minus the matched fp32-ft control (pp): w8a8 -0.08, w4a8 -0.81, w4a4 -13.22, w4a4-early8 -1.92, w3a8 -4.41, w2a8 -21.22.
- relevance-16-prune50 (counted, not measured): weights take 6,672 bytes in float and 1,776 at 8 bits; arithmetic per window is about 19.7 µJ in float and 1.28 µJ at 8/8, 0.207 µJ with the layer swap.

## Does the simulation reproduce ONNX Runtime INT8?

The simulated 8/8 network uses the grids of the archived ONNX Runtime INT8 graphs (per-channel 8-bit weights, min-max activation ranges from the same session-1 trials), so the two should agree.

- Predictions agree with the archived INT8 predictions on 99.29% of session-2 trials on average over the 459 models (lowest model 97.22%), and with the archived FP32 predictions on 96.97%.
- Accuracy differs from ONNX Runtime INT8 by 0.33 pp per model on average (largest 1.86 pp). Over participants, simulated minus ONNX Runtime INT8 is -0.04 [-0.09, +0.00] pp.
- Without any rounding, the folded network matches the archived FP32 accuracy to 0.00 pp per model on average.

Rank correlation (Spearman) of the session-1 and session-2 changes over these 20 cases: +0.89 (p = 1.2e-07).

Rule, from session 1 only: a tensor needs more bits when rounding it alone costs more than 2 points of training-trial accuracy, on average over participants.

- Activations that need more than 4 bits, so the rule keeps them at 8: input EEG, temporal convolution output, logits. The planned early-8 settings keep input EEG, temporal convolution output at 8 bits: the rule also keeps logits.
- Weights that need more than 4 bits, so the rule keeps them at 8: spatial convolution; every planned mixed setting rounds all weights to 4 bits or fewer.
- Weights that need more than 2 bits, so the rule keeps them at 4: temporal convolution, spatial convolution, pointwise convolution, classifier. The planned spatial-4 settings keep spatial convolution at 4 bits: the rule also keeps temporal convolution, pointwise convolution, classifier.

## Quantization-aware fine-tuning (4 architectures, 100 epochs, Adam, learning rate 0.0001)

Each variant starts from the archived model with its rounding switched on and trains for 100 more epochs on the session-1 training trials. fp32-ft trains the same epochs without rounding; it is the fair reference, because extra training alone changes accuracy. 'Before' is the same rounding without fine-tuning (PTQ); for fp32-ft it is the archived model itself.

## Cost of one inference (one 2-s window, batch 1; counted, not measured)

- Weight storage: weights x weight bits / 8, plus every bias at 32 bits, BatchNorm folded as deployed. Not included: one 32-bit scale per output channel of each rounded layer (weight_scale_bytes in costs.csv, 240 bytes for full-22) and one scale and zero point per activation tensor.
- Peak activation memory: the largest input + output pair of one layer (as in costs.py), each tensor at its own width.
- Bit-operations: MACs x weight bits x activation bits, floating point counted as 32 bits.
- Arithmetic energy, Horowitz (ISSCC 2014, 45 nm): an integer multiply costs 0.2 pJ at 8 bits, taken to scale with the product of the two widths (0.2 x w/8 x a/8 pJ, which gives 3.2 pJ at 32 bits against the reported 3.1); the accumulate is a 32-bit integer add, 0.1 pJ; a layer with floating-point weights or activations costs a float32 multiply and add, 3.7 + 0.9 pJ per MAC. Only MACs are counted. Memory traffic (reading weights and activations), which on real chips often costs more than the arithmetic, is not counted: treat the energy as an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measurement.
- Layer-swapped: the same function with the spatial filters first (results/supplementary/int8_study); its MACs are read from that study's costs.csv. Its energy is shown only where all weights share one width and all activations another.
